items.notes: A.T.P.CO, 'AUTHENTIC GARMENTS / Quality guaranteed', size 40. Italian label. Dark teal-green ground with a dense small-scale paisley and floral-medallion print - teardrop paisleys and round rosette medallions, roughly 20 to 25mm across, packed close with little visible ground between them, in mustard-ochre, mid blue, rust-red and cream outlines. HEX METHOD: taken from the _01 macro, the only frame with the cloth sharp and evenly lit, white-balanced against the woven white brand label in the same frame, giving a blended distance read of #535955. The two worn frames were both shot in shade and returned #30302E and #212427 - 30 to 50 levels too dark - so they were rejected rather than averaged in, the same call made on tops_33. Be aware the blended value reads as a dark greenish slate rather than as teal: the warm motifs neutralise the green when everything is averaged, which is exactly what happens to the eye at distance too Retail render 2026-08-27: Gemini returned square 1:1, ghost mannequin, spread collar at full length, barrel cuffs, AUTHENTIC GARMENTS neck tape kept, and it correctly produced a PAISLEY - teardrop boteh plus round rosettes in mustard, blue, rust and cream on a teal ground - rather than substituting a floral or a geometric, which was the named risk. Corrected: blended read came back at #494F51 against a measured #535955, so a per-channel gain was applied to the garment only, leaving the print structure and the shading intact; a two-point stripe curve was deliberately not used here because a print has no clean bimodal light/dark split to anchor on. Background clamped to pure #FFFFFF. Composed 2000x2000 and 1600x2000 at 8.5% margin. HONEST DEVIATION: the rendered motifs sit slightly larger and more spaced than the real cloth, which is denser with less ground showing between motifs. Good enough for catalogue identification, not a fabric-accurate swatch.

items.verdictNote: Bin. Max asked whether the pocket and the pattern make it read like a pyjama top. They do, and the useful answer is WHY, because it decides whether it is fixable. FOUR THINGS CREATE THE PYJAMA READ, not two. (1) STRIPE LAYOUT: evenly spaced single-colour pinstripes with regular wide gaps on a pale ground is ticking - the literal pattern of sleepwear. Dress-shirt stripes escape this by being either much denser, like tops_27's hairline which reads solid, or grouped and varied in width, like tops_33 and tops_34. This one sits in the exact middle where it looks like nightwear. (2) PATCH POCKET: a plain square patch with no flap and no shaping is a pyjama detail; note that tops_19, a proper dress shirt, is recorded as having no chest pocket at all. (3) SOFT UNSTRUCTURED COLLAR that flops rather than standing. (4) LOOSE CUT, and pyjamas are cut full. THE POCKET IS THE ONLY ONE THAT IS FIXABLE - a tailor removes it for 20 to 30 dollars, and on a striped cloth the shadow left behind hides in the pattern. But that is one of four, and the stripe layout is the biggest of them and cannot be changed. Add a body take-in and the bill reaches 60 to 80 dollars to rescue a shirt that still reads as sleepwear. IT ALSO FILLS NOTHING: pale blue is the most crowded colour in Tops, and tops_27 is a Paul Smith in the same colour that fits properly and is the best shirt in the catalogue

CONSISTENCY CHECK, because this shirt collides with two verdicts made earlier today and both need answering. AGAINST tops_38, binned for being polyester: that one is 100% polyester and sits unworn; this is a 65/35 poly-cotton blend, which breathes meaningfully better, and thirty years of actual wear in Sydney settles the comfort question far more reliably than any argument about fibre content. The empirical evidence beats the theory. AGAINST tops_30, the Cerruti, binned partly for being a dark-ground white pinstripe: the decisive fact there was Max saying he rarely wears it, with the pattern only supporting it. Here the decisive fact points the other way. The pattern also behaves differently at short sleeve with an open collar - it reads as a nineties casual shirt rather than a going-out dress shirt, and at thirty years old it is genuinely period rather than imitating one. IT ALSO MATTERS MORE THAN IT DID AN HOUR AGO: with tops_38 gone, short sleeve is down to this and tops_11, and this is the only dark one

items.notes: CORNWELL, size M, 39/40, 65% polyester / 35% cotton. Near-black with evenly spaced fine white pinstripes. MAX HAS OWNED IT ALMOST THIRTY YEARS AND STILL WEARS IT - that is recorded as the primary fact about this garment, not as colour. It is the oldest item in the catalogue by a wide margin and the only one whose verdict rests on longevity of use rather than on condition or cut. PLAN FOR ITS REPLACEMENT NOW RATHER THAN LATER: the polyester sheen is the failure mode that will eventually retire it, and when it does, the replacement should be deliberate - a dark short-sleeve shirt in cotton or linen. That sits alongside the short-sleeve gap flagged on tops_38 and is the same purchase. Buying it early also means the old one gets to finish its life rather than being worn past the point where it looks tired Retail render 2026-08-27 - USABLE BUT THE WEAKEST OF THE SESSION, AND WORTH REDOING. What went right: correct short sleeves with no cuffs and no buttons (the named risk, since every other shirt this session was long-sleeved), point collar, even single-width pinstripes, straight hem, tonal buttons, Cornwell neck label. TWO PROBLEMS, both stated plainly rather than papered over. (1) RESOLUTION: Gemini returned 1024x1024, not the 2048x2048 every other render came back at, so composing to 2000x2000 needed a 1.7x upscale and this file is visibly softer than the other six. (2) STRIPE COLOUR NOT RECOVERED: the render's pinstripes came back GREY at #9B9A9B against a measured cream #E4DFD3. The correction pass fixed the overall garment - blended converged on the measured #46474F exactly - but it could NOT lift the stripes, which stalled at #7F8189 after eight iterations. The reason is the resolution: at 1024px the stripes are about two pixels wide and fully anti-aliased, so there is no true stripe core left to anchor on, only stripe-and-ground blend. No tone curve can recover colour that was never resolved. Background was clamped to pure #FFFFFF successfully. RECOMMENDATION: regenerate this one at 2048x2048; both faults are the same fault and both go away with the resolution.

It fits now, it is clean, and pale grey reading as a plain solid makes it one of the more useful things in Tops - it goes with everything and it is the only pale grey shirt owned. Max also says he likes it and likes wearing short sleeves in summer, which settles it. ON THE POLYESTER QUESTION, since tops_38 was binned for exactly that: the two are not the same case. tops_38 was 100% polyester, boxy, Lowes house brand, and unworn. Here the composition is unknown rather than known-bad, the cut is good, and Max wears it and does not mind it - the same reasoning that kept tops_39. items.notes: CELIO CLUB, Taille M (39/40). French high-street brand - and note outerwear_02 is the jacket Max calls 'the Celio black wax jacket', so the name already appears in this wardrobe. Pale grey-white ground with a fine dark micro-hatch print, fine enough to read as a plain light grey from two metres. White contrast inner collar band and placket facing. Hex CORRECTED after a first bad sample: the initial reading of #4F5052 came from the _01 macro but the crop had landed on the shadowed inside of the shirt behind the placket rather than on the outer cloth, giving a value far too dark for a garment that is obviously pale grey. Re-sampled from the _02 hanger frame instead, averaging four separate regions - both sleeves, chest and skirt - each white-balanced against the wall behind, giving #9B9DA2. The lesson is the ordinary one: a number that disagrees with what the photograph plainly shows is a bad crop, not a discovery. Five frames supplied including two worn-front, both kept. THE CATEGORY PICTURE, WHICH IS THE REAL POINT OF THIS ENTRY: Max has now said outright that he likes short-sleeve shirts in summer and wants a few. He owns four. tops_38 has just been binned as 100% polyester. tops_39 is thirty years old and starting to sheen. tops_11 is recorded as snug through the chest with almost no seam allowance. This one is 'a bit tight'. That is four items, three of them at risk, in a category he actively wants, while he is actively bulking. Two or three short-sleeve shirts in cotton or linen should move to PRIORITY 1 on the shopping list - ahead of most of what is currently there, because this is a stated preference meeting a genuine shortage rather than a gap inferred from the spreadsheet Retail render 2026-08-27: back at 2048x2048 after an explicit resolution line was added to the prompt - that fix worked and the line should stay on every prompt from here. Correct short sleeves with no cuffs, point collar held, curved hem, white buttons, CELIO CLUB neck label, micro-print at the right minute scale, and both the white contrast collar band and the placket facing reproduced. TWO PROBLEMS, ONE OF THEM MINE. (1) Gemini ignored the pure-white background and returned a pale blue-grey ground (#F4F4F4). (2) My first correction pass then destroyed the render: the standard background mask keys on colour proximity, and because this shirt is pale grey sitting on a pale grey-blue ground the mask bled straight into the garment and cut away most of the right side and hem. The output was checked visually, the damage was obvious, and the pass was rebuilt. THE FIX, WORTH REUSING: separate background from garment on local TEXTURE rather than on colour - the flat background measured a local standard deviation of 0.75 against 34.5 for the printed cloth, a 45x separation where the colour difference was only about 36 levels - then flood from the frame border, fill holes, and dilate the garment mask slightly so the anti-aliased edge is not shaved off. Any pale garment on a non-white ground will hit this same trap. Corrected: garment blended #D0D1D1 against the measured #9B9DA2 via a per-channel gain on the garment only; background then clamped to pure #FFFFFF. Composed 2000x2000 and 1600x2000 at 8.5% margin.
